transcript.text: Hey, Alex. I own a coffee shop. I tried
going off grid for 7 days to see if the
business could run without me. Didn't
even make it to day three.
I realize I am the process for about
half the things that happen in my shop.
And if I got hit by a bus, this whole
thing fall apart. What do I do and where
do I even start?
>> key to getting your time back is getting
it back drop by drop not all at once.
You'll do something on a time study,
which basically means you set a timer
every 15 minutes throughout the day and
whenever it goes off, you open an Excel
sheet and you have the times per day and
you write down what you were doing or
what you did in the last 15 minutes.
Because what it's going to do is give
you full transparency into where your
time is going. And say, "Is there a
process, a person, or a project that I
need to create?" There's going to be
something that's the lowest ROI and then
you're going to have the second lowest
ROI and maybe it's a process or a
project. I want to get all my process
and projects off my plate that are the
lowest ROI first. So, after that I'm
going to look at the ones that I think
people are going to be solving. And so,
then I would follow up with people. And
all you're doing fundamentally is buying
back your time. I think where you get
stuck is when you try to buy everything
back at once with one person. It almost
never works because that's expecting
someone to have lived your entire life
and have all the skills as you on their
second day.
